title: Background reading
description: Official California ALPR and public-records background for organizer review.
body_md:
[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] Re-check every title, publisher, date and official link before publishing this page.

These are public California documents about automated license plate readers (ALPRs) and the state public records law. They are background reading, not findings about any agency, and not legal advice. Laws change, so check the current version of any statute before relying on it. The California law package shipped with this tool is a draft and has not been independently reviewed, and this list does not change that. This page is written for California even when your campaign is in another state, so do not read it as the law of any other state.

## Audit and guidance

**Automated License Plate Readers: To Better Protect Individuals’ Privacy, Law Enforcement Must Increase Its Safeguards for the Data It Collects**

Publisher: California State Auditor (report 2019-118)

Published: February 13, 2020

[Automated License Plate Readers: To Better Protect Individuals’ Privacy, Law Enforcement Must Increase Its Safeguards for the Data It Collects](https://information.auditor.ca.gov/pdfs/reports/2019-118.pdf)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This report examines ALPR privacy safeguards, data security, retention and oversight.

**California Automated License Plate Reader Data Guidance**

Publisher: California Department of Justice, Division of Law Enforcement (Information Bulletin 2023-DLE-06)

Issued: October 27, 2023

[California Automated License Plate Reader Data Guidance](https://www.oag.ca.gov/system/files/media/2023-dle-06.pdf)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This guidance bulletin describes the Department of Justice's guidance on the collection, storage, sharing and use of ALPR information and is guidance, not a statute.

## California statutes and public records

**Civil Code, Title 1.81.23. Collection of License Plate Information (sections 1798.90.5 to 1798.90.55)**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Effective: January 1, 2016

[Civil Code, Title 1.81.23. Collection of License Plate Information (sections 1798.90.5 to 1798.90.55)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?division=3.&lawCode=CIV&part=4.&title=1.81.23.)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This title of the Civil Code covers ALPR definitions, security and usage policies, access records and the rules for public agencies.

**Government Code section 7920.000**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Effective: January 1, 2022; operative January 1, 2023

[Government Code section 7920.000](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=7920.000.)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This section gives the California Public Records Act its short title.

**Government Code section 7922.530**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Effective: January 1, 2022; operative January 1, 2023

[Government Code section 7922.530](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=7922.530.)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This section covers copies of public records, duplication fees and conditions on requester equipment.

**Government Code section 7922.535**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Effective: January 1, 2026 (amended by Stats. 2025, ch. 34, AB 370)

[Government Code section 7922.535](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=7922.535.)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This section covers the agency determination on a request for copies of records and the written notice that extends that time in unusual circumstances.

**Government Code section 7923.000**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Effective: January 1, 2022; operative January 1, 2023

[Government Code section 7923.000](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=7923.000.)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This section covers court proceedings to enforce the right to inspect or receive public records.

## Legislative background

**SB 34 (Hill), Automated license plate recognition systems: use of data, Senate Floor Analysis (Unfinished Business)**

Publisher: California State Senate, Office of Senate Floor Analyses, on the Legislature's leginfo site

Analysis date: September 3, 2015

[SB 34 (Hill), Automated license plate recognition systems: use of data, Senate Floor Analysis (Unfinished Business)](https://leginfo.ca.gov/pub/15-16/bill/sen/sb_0001-0050/sb_34_cfa_20150903_180229_sen_floor.html)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This legislative analysis describes the proposed ALPR privacy and usage requirements as the bill stood after Assembly amendments and is historical background, not current law.

**AB 370, California Public Records Act: cyberattacks (Chapter 34, Statutes of 2025)**

Publisher: California Legislative Information, Office of Legislative Counsel

Approved: July 14, 2025

[AB 370, California Public Records Act: cyberattacks (Chapter 34, Statutes of 2025)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB370)

[EDIT ME: verify for this campaign] This chaptered bill with its Legislative Counsel's Digest covers the amendment of the California Public Records Act provisions on extending the time to respond when a cyberattack or an emergency is involved.
